Assessing Our Results
■ What are the trends over time?
■ What are the trends for groups?

■ How did overall achievement change,

compared to the same students’ achievement
last year?
■ How does the change compare to a standards-

based or norms-based idea of a year’s growth?
■ How does the change differ by groups?

■ How do achievement data compare with school

climate, parent, staff and NCG survey results?

A Relatively New Metric: Colorado’s Growth
Model

■ Easier to use and understand than
the previous methods
■ Supported by a useful video

■ CDE graphs available online by

district and school
■ Current year results arrived at a later

than ideal time for full use

Colorado Median Growth Percentile
■ Amount of gain is statistically compared
across students starting from the same
point (“academic peers”)
■ Growth percentile assigned: percent of

“academic peers” making that amount of
gain or less
■ Percentiles range from 1 to 99, can be

compared with state median of 50
■ Accountability Measure: the middle growth

%-ile

Productive Response to Median
Growth Percentile
■ Users are far less dismissive of gaps
in growth than in achievement
■ Because a student’s growth is not

readily predicted, raising median
growth requires group improvement
■ Reflection on what went well for

students with high growth

School and Teacher Use
■ Fair comparison across content
areas
■ Encouraged for use in school goal

setting, especially around equity
■ Published at student level in Student

Information System (Infinite
Campus), contextualized with
grades, demographics, simple gain

Avoiding Over-Interpretation

■ Contextualize with Error Estimates
■ Examine Multiple Content Areas

and Years of Results for Each
Student
■ Consider Likely Response of

Parents, Having Seen Percentiles
only for Achievement, not Growth
